A service that already exists on a Windows host: how it starts and whether it's running. Removing the step leaves it as it is.

Use `windows_service` to say how an existing service starts and whether it's running. Conn3x doesn't create services here.

## Example usage

```hcl
step "web_running" {
  windows_service {
    name       = "W3SVC"
    start_mode = "auto"
    state      = "running"
  }
}
```

```hcl
step "no_print_spooler" {
  windows_service {
    name       = "Spooler"
    start_mode = "disabled"
    state      = "stopped"
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Service name, not its display name, such as W3SVC. |
| `start_mode` | string | No | "auto", "delayed", "manual" or "disabled". Left as it is when unset. |
| `state` | string | No | "running" or "stopped". Left as it is when unset. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_windows_service.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the service matched at the last refresh. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_windows_service` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.

## How it works

Use the service's name, not its display name, which changes with the display language. Stopping a service that others depend on fails with Windows' message: stop those first. A service that stops right after starting shows as an error at apply, not a success.

Be careful with `sshd`. Stopping or disabling it cuts Conn3x off from the host.

## Removal

Deleting a `windows_service` step leaves the service as it is.
